title: HapticGuide: Interactive Wearable Braille Guide for Enhancing Visual Education
problem: Visually impaired students struggle to understand complex spatial and geometric concepts due to limitations of traditional tactile graphics and physical models, which lack dynamic, real-time feedback mechanisms.
motivation: Traditional assistive technologies for geometric education are static and do not provide interactive guidance. A dynamic, wearable haptic system can enable students to receive real-time directional feedback while tracing shapes, improving spatial understanding and cognitive mapping.
method: When a student touches a 15×15 grid made from Velostat pressure sensors and copper strips, the cloud system instantly detects that touch location. The cloud maps the touch position to a specific vibration pattern and sends it to five coin vibration motors embedded in a wearable glove. As the motors vibrate against the student's fingers, they provide real-time tactile feedback that lets the student feel the spatial relationships and shapes.
key_novelty: The core idea is to pair a touch-sensitive grid with vibration feedback that's coordinated through the cloud in real-time, letting visually impaired students learn geometry interactively through their fingers.
contributions: Design of a low-cost, portable haptic wearable device for geometric shape tracing
Cloud-based synchronization system for remote learning
Demonstration of improved spatial understanding in visually impaired learners
limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative performance metrics provided; scalability of 15×15 grid not analyzed; cloud latency impact not discussed; limited to geometric education domain.
